scope: Read existing generated Metal and frozen timing events; no build, GPU run or parameter change.
allocation_observer: newBufferWithLength:options: calls returning a buffer; counts, not bytes or caller/pool attribution

confirmed: MTF removes two pointwise device fields and keeps all three mixed values thread-local; its combined MTF kernels have no for-loop or pow expression.
Coupler removes Released but retains the downsample grid; release/curve expressions move into dynamic box reductions, which remain in generated Metal even though the measured requests have stride1.
MTF UHD steady new-buffer calls fall from about4/frame to exactly1/frame in all three rounds; Coupler UHD stays at exactly4/frame in all Fused rounds.
The pool rounds sizes, uses exact bucket matching and caps idle retained bytes; eliminating a logical field does not guarantee fewer future allocations or a lower retained total.
interpretation.supported_explanation: MTF removes cheap pointwise boundaries without adding sampling loops, and reduces both large-field traffic and observed fresh-buffer churn. Coupler retains the generic reduction structure and observed churn. This explains why the first experiment has stronger evidence of practical gains, but does not quantify the contribution of each cost.
not_established: No per-kernel GPU time, DRAM traffic, physical register allocation or spill counters were collected.

Source for/pow counts are static and include alternate branches/specializations; they are not per-pixel executed instruction counts. Gamma1 in the measured profiles may be optimized further by the Metal compiler.
The buffer observer records neither byte sizes nor allocation call ancestry, so exact pool misses/evictions and allocation-time contribution are not proven.
Two separate timing campaigns cannot be used as a direct performance comparison of their fused arms.
interpretation.next_hypothesis: For Coupler stride1, investigate a dedicated identity-grid path or specialization instead of carrying generic reduction loops. Preserve release-before-average for strides greater than1; not implemented or benchmarked here.
